may: locate, copy, hash, classify, and admit donor artifacts
record rights, claim boundaries, failure states, and missing evidence
reject a donor whose identity, provenance, or integrity cannot be reproduced
may_not: promote a donor into the successor interface
treat a located artifact as archived
close JDB99-001 while any required custody gap remains open
alter the historical public Manzanita route during custody work

qualification_boundary: A passing custody validation proves only that the register, repo-resident hashes, route guard, and declared gaps are internally consistent. It does not close JDB99-001, qualify a Manzanita release, or transfer product authority.

hash_law.manifest_encoding: UTF-8 canonical JSON with sorted keys

public_route_guard.failure_message: Any mismatch means custody work changed or failed to recover the historical public route. Stop integration and investigate before merging.

donors.claim_boundary: Historical public donor. Its own qualification receipt is preserved, but the 99-point program does not admit it as the successor or as whole-product qualified.

donors.location: git history, retained receipt, and owner-only Google Drive archive
donors.claim_boundary: Qualified source-foundation donor only. The exact 41-file artifact is privately archived and verified, but the live acquisition claim remains bound to the preserved pre-rebase head and workflow run. The rebased head requires its own admitted checks, and the private archive still needs an independently controlled mirror for final cold-successor closure.
Planning donor absorbed into the canonical backlog. It carries no product-completion claim.
Constitution and execution overlay only. These records do not qualify a product surface.
Receipt for the repository Pages deployment, not proof that every route or release is qualified.

gaps.target: Enumerate and retain every Manzanita release and failed build before 1.4.0 from git history and any surviving external package.
gaps.admission: Each release has an immutable commit or package identity, complete file manifest, SHA-256 hashes, classification, and claim boundary.
gaps.failure_mode: A visually or functionally important predecessor disappears behind the label 'old version'.

gaps.target: Download and ingest the 41-file artifact from workflow run 31903077053, including all 20 source receipts and retained payloads.
gaps.admission: The ZIP bytes, expanded files, per-file SHA-256 hashes, source times, requests, rights fields, and artifact identity are retained outside expiring Actions storage.
gaps.failure_mode: The qualified live-data claim survives only as prose after the Actions retention window expires.
gaps.closure: GitHub artifact 9251615986 was downloaded before expiry. Its 8,639,908 bytes matched SHA-256 c83cebc5a2c6266fa14f77db2758ec25d86cca86e69630a42ce08dcfafa99e9e; all 41 ZIP entries, 20 source receipts, and declared payload hashes were verified; an owner-only Google Drive copy was written and read back.

gaps.target: Locate every approved and rejected Manzanita visual golden, including full-state desktop, mobile, compact, light, dark, and failure views.
gaps.admission: Each image is tied to route, commit, viewport, theme, state, browser, capture method, and acceptance or rejection disposition.
gaps.failure_mode: Later work can imitate a hero crop while losing the state that was actually approved or rejected.

gaps.target: Recover playtest scripts, seat transcripts, observed failures, and disposition records for the v1.4 and rejected v1.5 sequences.
gaps.admission: Every finding names the seat, scenario, build identity, observation, severity, disposition, and retained evidence.
gaps.failure_mode: A later build repeats a known failure because only the summary survived.

gaps.target: Retain failed CI runs, deployment failures, rejected-release receipts, and no-coverage or provider-failure artifacts that materially changed the design.
gaps.admission: Each failure has a stable run or file identity, logs or bounded extract, affected commit, classification, and resulting rule.
gaps.failure_mode: Successful reruns erase the causal evidence for the rule that followed.

gaps.target: Retain every admitted live-data acquisition bundle beyond PR #90, including empty, stale, contradictory, missing-credential, rate-limited, and outage states.
gaps.admission: Payloads and receipts preserve request, response class, source time, retrieval time, transform, attribution, rights, cache rule, uncertainty, and degradation state.
gaps.failure_mode: Only the happy-path payload remains available for qualification.

gaps.target: Backfill Manzanita-specific deployment receipts and exact public-byte identities for prior releases and failed deployments.
gaps.admission: Every deployed or attempted release has source commit, artifact digest, endpoint, run identity, outcome, rollback target, and observed public hash.
gaps.failure_mode: Repository state is mistaken for the bytes that actually reached the endpoint.

gaps.target: Locate original sourced, captured, authored, modeled, generated, and transformed visual assets with rights and claim receipts.
gaps.admission: Each asset has original bytes or stable source, creator or provider, acquisition date, rights class, transforms, generated-state label where applicable, and permitted claims.
gaps.failure_mode: A polished image becomes an unattributed orphan or is later mistaken for observed evidence.

gaps.target: Locate standalone Manzanita HTML, ZIP, PDF, image, and handoff exports that existed outside the current repository tree.
gaps.admission: Each export has complete bytes, SHA-256, production date, source build, purpose, recipient class, and supersession status.
gaps.failure_mode: An externally circulated artifact cannot be reproduced or distinguished from the canonical route.

gaps.target: Mirror the exact PR #90 source-foundation ZIP into the independently controlled local estate or a second durable archive.
gaps.admission: The mirror retains the same 8,639,908 bytes and SHA-256 c83cebc5a2c6266fa14f77db2758ec25d86cca86e69630a42ce08dcfafa99e9e, has a documented recovery path, and is replayed by a cold successor.
gaps.failure_mode: The only durable copy remains contingent on access to one Google account, so account loss defeats succession despite successful content hashing.
